title: Nebula Insurance — claim-bot pilot: call notes & immediate actions
content:
Context:
Call with Nebula Insurance (prod PM + infra + security) to scope a 6-week pilot for a conversational claim intake assistant ("claim-bot"). Nebula wants low-touch integration with existing claim workflow (CRM: ClaimTrack) and strict PHI handling (HIPAA). They asked about hosted vs private options and rough cost/latency tradeoffs.

Attendees:
- Derek Walker (Nebula, PM)
- Luis Andrade (Nebula, infra)
- Priya Shah (Nebula, security/compliance)
- Maya Chen (Redwood, SE)
- Ethan Rivera (Redwood, Solutions)
- Samir Gupta (Redwood, SRE/infra)

High-level ask from Nebula:
- Pilot: ~10k monthly interactions, peak concurrency ~25 reqs/min, typical session = 8 turns, avg tokens/user ~450 (incoming+generated)
- Latency SLO: 200ms p50 for single-turn (soft), 500ms p95 (hard).
- Strict no-PHI exfiltration to third-party services; customer-owned keys preferred.
- Audit logs and redaction: ability to strip/obfuscate SSNs and bank account numbers before logging.
- Simple integration path: webhook / REST call to ClaimTrack to create or update claim records; fallback to manual triage if model confidence < threshold.
- Cost target: <$0.10 per end-user session (ballpark).

Key technical notes / gotchas raised on call:
1) Data flow & PHI: Priya insisted on no plaintext PHI leaving Nebula VPC. They are open to Redwood Private with a customer-managed control plane or an on-prem agent for PII redaction. Action: need a short runbook we can hand to their infra team showing options (private control plane + KMS integration vs hosted with tokenization proxy).

2) Model choice vs latency/cost: Nebula will likely prefer a smaller quantized model (13B or 7B) to hit latency/cost targets. They asked whether Redwood supports warmed KV caching for repeated policy text (lots of identical boilerplate per claim). Confirmed: yes — we can configure prefix caching for policy/FAQ prompts which will reduce token count.

3) Confidence metric & routing: They want a deterministic fallback if the model is "unsure". We suggested a confidence heuristic using token-level probabilities + a reranker for final outputs. Also proposed a simple rule: if model_confidence < 0.6 OR entity-extraction fallback fails -> route to human triage. Need to document suggested thresholds and a small eval set.

4) Audit + retention: Their compliance team wants ability to redact PII before storing logs and also to keep an immutable audit trail for last 90 days. Option: run redaction hooks in the private enclave prior to log emission. Need to confirm log retention policy mapping in Redwood Console.

5) Network egress & certs: Luis asked about mutual TLS and private peering options. He prefers private peering over internet egress. Redwood: we have VPC peering options for Private deployments; for Hosted, we can support an IP allowlist and MTLS with customer certs.

6) Claims schema alignment: ClaimTrack schema has ~120 fields; only ~12 are needed for the initial MVP. We'll ship a mapping doc (fields -> prompt variables). We must validate redaction for fields marked PHI.

7) Eval dataset: Nebula can provide 150 dev transcripts and 50 red-team transcripts (PHI masked) to calibrate QA and coverage. Ask: need format spec for transcripts (CSV vs JSONL).

Proposed pilot scope (6 weeks):
- Week 0: Kickoff + network setup (1 week) — decide on Private vs Hosted with tokenization proxy.
- Week 1–2: Integration & mapping (2 weeks) — ClaimTrack webhook mapping, entity schemas, redaction rules, sample dataset ingestion.
- Week 3: Model selection & tuning (1 week) — test 7B vs 13B variants, latency/cost measurements, configure KV caching and batching.
- Week 4: Canary + run small live -> 1000 sessions (1 week) — collect metrics, safety evals.
- Week 5–6: Iterate on thresholds, logging, and handoff plan.

Rough resource estimate (pilot):
- Redwood SE time: 0.2 FTE (Maya/Ethan) for 6 weeks (kickoff, weekly syncs, integration support)
- Redwood infra/SRE: 0.05 FTE (Samir) for network + private deploy support
- Nebula infra + security: expected 0.3 FTE during Week 0–2
- Cloud/GPU: If private -> customer-managed, cost on Nebula. If hosted -> estimate $1k–2k for the 6-week pilot depending on model and peak.

Open questions (need answers from Nebula):
- Which deployment mode? (Preferred: Private control plane w/ Redwood runtime or hosted with tokenization proxy?)
- Can Nebula provide the 200 anonymized transcripts and schema by 2026-03-05 to keep the timeline?
- Confirm retention window and who owns the audit logs.
- Are there regulatory reviewers who need to pre-approve prompts or will Redwood redaction suffice?

Immediate next steps (owners + ETA):
- Create and share a 1-page runbook for deployment options (Private vs Hosted w/ tokenization) — Maya (Redwood) — ETA 2026-03-03.
- Provide transcript format spec (JSONL schema example) + sample file — Ethan (Redwood) — ETA 2026-03-02.
- Draft ClaimTrack field mapping template (12 MVP fields) and share for review — Derek + Maya — ETA 2026-03-06.
- Small latency/cost estimate comparing 7B vs 13B quantized options (with KV caching on) — Samir — ETA 2026-03-04.
- Security sync to confirm KMS/HSM support and redaction placement — Priya (Nebula) + Priya Shah to coordinate; Redwood SEs to join — set meeting 2026-03-05.

Risks / Mitigations:
- Risk: PHI leaves environment if hosted path chosen. Mitigation: recommend Private control plane or deploy tokenization proxy inside Nebula network (we can provide reference container).
- Risk: Latency targets might be missed during peak if using larger models. Mitigation: start with 7B quantized + aggressive prefix caching; measure and move up only if quality insufficient.
- Risk: Cost creep with long conversations. Mitigation: enforce turn limits and encourage short-form responses + post-processing to reduce token generation.

Notes to self (quick):
- Prepare a short demo script using ClaimTrack sample data; show redaction hook in action and fallback to human triage when confidence low.
- Add a small eval harness in repo: nebula-integration-prototype/evals to run 200 examples and generate confidence histograms.
- Check existing private-deploy templates for mutual TLS example (repo/team: private-deploy/mTLS-sample).

Meeting artifacts to attach after follow-up:
- network diagram (VPC peering vs tokenization-proxy)
- example redaction regex rules + mapping table
- eval results (7B vs 13B) with p50/p95 latency and per-session cost estimate

Longer-term thoughts (brainstorm):
- Potential for a "claims-optimized" quantization profile: small model tweaked on historical non-PHI claim language to improve compression and safety. Worth exploring post-pilot.
- Add a lightweight reranker that runs on a CPU tier to validate named-entity consistency before commit to ClaimTrack (cheap safety filter).

Status: standing up internal PRD draft after Maya shares runbook. Follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-05 (security sync).

-- Maya
